title: The logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The course is the start of an exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality for convex bodies that are symmetric about the origin: the Wulff body of the geometric mean of two support functions has volume at least the geometric mean of the volumes. The first lesson proves the facts about support functions and Wulff bodies that are needed, and proves that the inequality in dimension n follows from a variance bound for explicit smooth probability densities (soft polytopes), by a second derivative of the logarithm of an integral and three limits; it also derives the additive inequality for powers between 0 and 1. The variance bound itself is not yet in the course.
prerequisites: the Lebesgue integral in R^n with the theorems of dominated and monotone convergence (core course Measure and Integration)
compact convex sets in R^n and Hoelder's inequality for finite sums; the lesson proves the facts about support functions that it uses

checks.reading: The manuscript 'The logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski conjecture' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026) was read in full on 12 Oct 2026 (eight sections of TeX); a first-pass check of its steps, with three check programs, is recorded in plan/OPENAI_091_SCOPING_20261012.md. Lesson 1 was written against Sections 1, 2 and 8.1. Every step was derived: the support-function facts (the manuscript uses them without proof; the lesson proves them, including the description of a convex body by its supporting half-spaces through a nearest point); the formula (log Z)'' = Var - E V''; the limits q to infinity (dominated convergence), eps to 0 (monotone convergence) and finitely many directions to all directions (continuity from above); dimension one; the corollary for 0 < p < 1. Example 2.1 (boxes with the same axes: the Wulff body is the box of the geometric means, with equality) and the four exercises are additions; their statements were verified by hand, Exercise 7.2 also numerically (plan/checks_20261012/lb_check_variance.py: E y^q = Var y^q = 1/q for q = 2, 4, 6, 10). No discrepancy with the manuscript.
checks.layout: Measured on 12 Oct 2026 in the staged reader at 1100, 768, 543 and 375 px: lesson 1 has 398 formulas, 0 rendering errors, 0 wide formulas, no sideways page scroll.

open_obligations: Not yet in the course: the proof of the variance bound (Sections 3 to 7 of the manuscript: moment coordinates, adjoint identities, density of the even tests, the tensor estimate, the two Cauchy-Schwarz steps) and the corollary for even log-concave measures (Section 8.2). Until then the theorem of the first lesson is conditional: it proves the inequality from the variance bound.

The manuscript's proof of the variance bound uses results that the programme does not have: the moment theorem of Berman and Berndtsson for a density on a convex body, Klartag's bound for the Hessian of the moment potential, interior estimates for fully nonlinear and linear elliptic equations (Evans-Krylov, Schauder), and interior regularity for a fourth-order elliptic operator. They will be named hypotheses of the course.
Relayed and not checked: the statements about the history of the conjecture (attributed to the manuscript in the first lesson).
